title: BoardScreen is a 1,994-line file with one ~1,100-line component
note: BoardScreen.tsx is 1,994 lines; Board() runs 173-1260 (~1,088 lines). Render-time ref writes confirmed at 311, 313, 315, 332, 458, 842. BoardScreen.test.tsx has 5,871 lines, 17 vi.mock, 185 tests. Leaf components (HubButton 1703, Chips 1750, SummaryLine 1826, IdleFold 1901, Skeleton 1947, EmptyBoard 1977) are already module-level functions, so step 1 is a pure move.

title: Hold-or-send policy for Board actions written four times in BoardScreen and again in BoardReplay
note: The hold-vs-send branch is repeated at BoardScreen.tsx:597, 611, 640, 650, 956, but holdsChange (592) is already the single shared predicate, and the toast messages are already shared constants (SHUT_DOWN_DONE, RENAMED, shutDownFailed, renameFailed in rowActions.ts:140-150) and shutDownSession/renameSession are shared. The claim that online and replay 'build the same toasts separately' is false. The online and replay sends are not the same behavior: boardReplay.ts:117-150 does a fenced thread/read, a turnStillSeen drop (SHUT_DOWN_DROPPED), connection-drop detection and keep-held on loss; the online path in BoardScreen has none of that. A single shared send(action, client) would either regress replay safety or add it to online sends (a behavior change). The real remaining duplication is the small per-handler hold branch plus archiveRow/archiveRequest living in rowSwipes.ts.
revised_fix_plan: Do not unify online and replay sends. After finding 1 extracts useBoardActions, fold the four handlers' 'holdsChange(...) ? holdAction(...) : send' shape into one local helper (about -40 lines), and move archiveRow/archiveRequest from rowSwipes.ts to rowActions.ts. Keep boardReplay.ts untouched. Guard with existing rowActions/boardReplay/boardHold tests.

title: Native dialog helpers inlined in BoardScreen; copy and 80-char validation duplicated elsewhere
note: Two confirmShutDown exist with different copy (BoardScreen.tsx:1396 takes a row title; SessionInfoSheet.tsx:70 does not). The 80 code-point bound appears at BoardScreen.tsx:1264, PinAssignmentScreen.tsx:87, PinSectionEditorScreen.tsx:58, PinAssignmentEditor.tsx:44, and also on web at cmd/evener-hub/frontend/src/shell/rail/Rail.tsx:1758 ([...name].length > 80), which the finding missed and which strengthens the shared-constant plan. 'Use 1-80 characters' copy at two editors confirmed. The title-bearing signature difference means the two confirmShutDown need a title param (optional) to merge.

title: Board state derived by three hand-maintained native copies plus shared/web copies, already disagreeing
note: Drift verified against the hub: hubapi/attention.go:16 AttentionState turns approval_pending into 'awaiting' for every state except errored, shared railSessionState.ts:22 approvalWaiting does the same ('approval waiting'), and web railNodes.ts:384 displayState follows it. Native attention.ts:104 returns the decisive state (restartNeeded) before the approval check, and sessionState.ts:52-55 does the same, so native diverges from hub/web for restartRequired + approval_pending. The three native ladders (boardState, searchResultMark, sessionStateLine) also differ among themselves (searchResultMark has no offline, warning-yield or subagent-working rules), so duplication is real. Native imports nothing from railSessionState (grep empty). Severity lowered: the user-visible difference is confined to an edge combination, and native comment at sessionState.ts:41-46 shows the precedence may have been chosen deliberately to match NeedsYouBand.
revised_fix_plan: Ask Jesse first whether restartRequired/ended + approval_pending should read as approval (hub AttentionState) or restart needed (current native). Then add one pure attentionState() in appwire-client beside railSessionState.ts and make boardState/searchResultMark/sessionStateLine adapters, with one shared table test. Keep native-only nuances (offline, warning yielding to live children) in boardState explicitly.

title: Timestamp, duration, plural and minute-ticker helpers reinvented repeatedly
note: Confirmed: attention.ts:323 durationLabel feeds relativeAge a fabricated epoch ISO string to reuse its buckets (comment 319-322 admits the trick) while compactDuration from session/format is already imported at line 15; spokenAge (BoardRow.tsx:97) has its own UNITS map beside spokenDuration (format.ts:28); plural() exists at attention.ts:279 while inline 'count === 1 ?' ternaries sit at sessionState.ts:178, sessionFacts.ts:74/131/208, sessionNotes.ts:38, format.ts:34, BoardRow.tsx:103, transcriptRows.ts:563; Board has its own setInterval(MINUTE) at BoardScreen.tsx:145 beside useMinuteClock (a global ticker, not focus-gated, so replacement needs care). Overstated: the Date.parse helpers are not identical. hubTime returns number|null, trayLine.timeOf and delegateDetails.timestamp return undefined, sessionDocuments.time returns -Infinity for a deliberate sort-oldest meaning, and delegateDetails lives in the shared package so native hubTime cannot replace it. boardHold.ts:144 Date.parse is a one-off on a nullable value, not a duplicate parser. The cross-package unification to appwire-client would still be reasonable but is smaller than claimed.
revised_fix_plan: Delete durationLabel in favor of compactDuration (verify via attention.test that the 3m+ quiet strings are unchanged); make spokenAge reuse spokenDuration; export plural from one module and use it at the inline sites; make trayLine and subagentModel import hubTime (adapt null vs undefined at the two sites). Leave sessionDocuments.time and delegateDetails.timestamp alone. Only replace the Board's interval with useMinuteClock if focus gating is preserved. About -40 / +10.

title: 'May be stuck'/quiet text and thresholds defined twice; tray redefines the shared STUCK_AFTER_MS
note: trayLine.ts:27 exports STUCK_AFTER_MS = 10 * 60_000, identical to appwire-client sessionActivity.ts:11, which is exported from index.ts:577. The tray builds 'May be stuck · no updates for ${compactDuration(silence)}' at trayLine.ts:94 while attention.ts:367 builds the same sentence via durationLabel. A change to the shared threshold would move the Board (quietState) but not the tray. Fix is safe and small.

title: Hand-rolled subscribe/listeners/revision store repeated 14 times in the slice (~37 files repo-wide)
note: Grep in mobile-native/src finds 40 non-test files with listeners sets and 62 subscribe definitions. Each of the 12 listed files contains the Set<() => void>/listeners pattern. Drift visible: boardHold.ts:218-222 uses a block-bodied unsubscribe, detailLevels.ts uses an expression-bodied one that returns the delete boolean. No shared Subscribable exists in appwire-client or mobile-native (grep empty). Plan is sound but low value per file; do it opportunistically when touching each class.

title: Two seen-systems and several older-hub fallbacks that need Jesse's decision before deletion
note: Evidence quotes confirmed (attention.ts:66-70 approvalRefs 'a hub without S2a never sets that flag'; boardMemory.ts 'S4 replaces this with a marker on the hub'; activityPoll.ts method-not-found stops polling; boardData.ts:426 Jesse 'no client-side fallback' for notices). But the plan lumps in code that is not older-hub compat. workingActivity (attention.ts:399) is documented as the fallback for 'an older hub, before the first poll, or while disconnected', so deleting it breaks ordinary no-read states on current hubs. SeenMarkers also decides rows with no readable turn_ended_at (hubSeen.ts hubTurnEnd comment: 'a row without a readable turn_ended_at is the device's to decide'), which can occur for a brand-new session on a current hub, so it is not purely legacy. Only approvalRefs, tracksSeenThrough and the ActivityPoll unsupported flag are clearly hub-version compat. Adding a compat floor is a decision for Jesse, per his rules; the finding correctly says to ask first.
revised_fix_plan: Ask Jesse one question: is the app expected to talk only to hubs shipping S2a/S4/S5? If yes, delete approvalRefs, tracksSeenThrough and the unsupported flag; for seen, first prove (with a test) whether a current hub can send a row without turn_ended_at before collapsing BoardSeen. Keep workingActivity as the no-read-yet fallback, minus its older-hub wording. If no, record the floor in docs/product and annotate fallbacks. Do not start before the answer.

title: Comments narrate plan rulings, review rounds, issue numbers and people; stale file:line cites
note: Recounted over non-test, non-TestUtils files in board/ and session/ (125 files): 'ruling N' 81, 'rulings' 5, 'spec N' 164, '#NNN+' 42, 'RoboRev' 13, 'Jesse' 13. Stale cites confirmed: rowActions.ts:43 cites ProjectsScreen.tsx:749-757 (that region is unrelated code; the rule lives near line 625-631), rowActions.ts:153/158 cite conversation.ts:1128-1132 / 1197-1201 while the requests are at mobile/src/services/conversation.ts:911 and 979. evidence.ts:250 'a compatibility decision that needs Jesse's approval' and nativeConversationSessions.ts:42 'moves the screen's former backoff' are history/process narration. boardHold.ts:2 quotes Jesse inline. The proposed lint script keyed to 'ruling [0-9]' is borderline YAGNI; the mechanical comment cleanup is the valuable part.
revised_fix_plan: Do the comment pass file by file as files are touched by other findings (keep the invariant, drop ruling/spec/round/issue numbers, people and dates, replace file:line with symbol names). Record durable decisions in an evergreen docs/product section. Skip the new lint script unless Jesse asks.

title: NativeConversationSession exposes a test-only surface and a second read-retry loop
note: Confirmed: readSettled, attachmentCount, retired, entryFor, displayConfig, liveHost have no non-test reader (grep), and readActor.getFailures is the only member screens.tsx:774 uses. But these are heavily test-observed (readSettled() 10 test uses; the other members about 50 test uses), so the 'unused' members are the tests' observation seam, and removal means rewriting tests that assert fenced late-reply behavior. reconnectDelay is used in 7 non-test files (navigationPages, hubModels, usePinNavigation, boardSearch, useBoardReadRetry, nativeConversationSessions, hubConnection definition, outboxFlush), but the loops differ in what they cancel and fence, so a shared Backoff helper is speculative. Net: modest cleanup with risk in subtle generation logic.
revised_fix_plan: Only if touching the file: drop the interface members that have no test use at all, and leave readSettled and tested accessors. Do not introduce a Backoff abstraction without first diffing the loops and showing at least three are identical.

title: Per-hub persisted memory built four different ways
note: forgetBoard (boardMemory.ts:216-233) hand-rolls the try-all-then-throw loop that deviceStorage.removeKeys implements (its comment says 'the way forgetBoard does'). nativeDetailLevels.ts uses a raw Map while 6 other modules use perHub. DetailLevels (detailLevels.ts) and sessionNotes.ts:86-108 use raw JSON.parse/setItemSync. Caveat for the plan: forgetNoteDrafts currently swallows storage errors via writeDrafts (unlike removeKeys, which throws), so switching it to removeKeys changes behavior and needs a test. FoldedSections listener claim not independently checked beyond a grep showing no listeners.

title: Board shutdown/rename/stop requests re-implemented beside the Session's own
note: Request sites confirmed: mobile/src/services/conversation.ts:911 and 979, frontend threads.ts:8067 and 8180, native rowActions.ts shutDownSession/renameSession. Each is a single typed client.request call; wrapping them in shared helpers adds a layer for one line each (pass-through wrapper). The real defect is the rotted file:line cites (covered by finding 10). BoardStops (boardStops.ts:1-12, 112-170) does mirror the Session stop sequence by design and its header says so; a parity test is a reasonable guard but not a refactor.
revised_fix_plan: Skip the shutdownThread/renameThread helpers. Remove the stale conversation.ts line cites (finding 10). Optionally add one test driving Board Stop and Session Stop over the same recorded wire and comparing the outbox record.
